items.informal_name: Integral Element Criterion via Monic Polynomial Evaluation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] {x : A}
  {p : Polynomial R}, p.Monic → p.natDegree ≠ 0 → IsIntegral R ((Polynomial.aeval x) p) → IsIntegral R x
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative ring, $ A $ an $ R $-algebra, and $ x \in A $. If $ p \in R[X] $ is a monic polynomial of positive degree such that $ p(x) $ is integral over $ R $, then $ x $ is integral over $ R $.

items.informal_name: Degree of Polynomial with Irrational Root is Greater Than One
items.type: ∀ (x : ℝ) (p : Polynomial ℤ), Irrational x → p ≠ 0 → (Polynomial.aeval x) p = 0 → 1 < p.natDegree
items.informal_description: Let $ p $ be a non-zero polynomial with rational coefficients, and let $ x $ be an irrational real number such that $ p(x) = 0 $. Then the degree of $ p $ satisfies $ \deg(p) > 1 $.

items.informal_name: Minimal Polynomial Degree at Least Two iff Element Not in Algebra Map Image
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} {B : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : Ring B] [inst_2 : Algebra A B] {x : B} [Nontrivial B],
  IsIntegral A x → (2 ≤ (minpoly A x).natDegree ↔ x ∉ (algebraMap A B).range)
items.informal_description: For an element $ x $ in $ B $ that is integral over $ A $, the natural degree of the minimal polynomial $ \minpoly_A(x) $ satisfies $ 2 \leq \deg(\minpoly_A(x)) $ if and only if $ x $ is not in the image of the canonical algebra homomorphism $ \mathrm{algebraMap}: A \to B $. Here, $ \deg(\minpoly_A(x)) $ denotes the natural degree of the minimal polynomial, which is the degree of the polynomial if it is non-zero and 0 otherwise.

items.informal_name: Existence of Monic Quadratic Polynomial with Root in Real Normed Algebra
items.type:
∀ {F : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing F] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℝ F] [NormOneClass F] [NormMulClass F] (x : F),
  ∃ p, p.IsMonicOfDegree 2 ∧ (Polynomial.aeval x) p = 0
items.informal_description: For every element $ x $ in a real normed algebra $ F $, there exists a monic polynomial $ p $ of degree 2 with real coefficients such that $ p(x) = 0 $.

items.informal_name: Integral Element Criterion via Monic Polynomial Evaluation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_4} {A : Type u_5} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] {x : A}
  {p : Polynomial A},
  p.Monic →
    p.natDegree ≠ 0 → IsIntegral R (Polynomial.eval x p) → (∀ (i : ℕ), IsIntegral R (p.coeff i)) → IsIntegral R x
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ and $ A $ be commutative rings with $ A $ an $ R $-algebra. If $ p \in A[X] $ is a monic polynomial of positive degree such that each coefficient of $ p $ is integral over $ R $, and $ p(x) $ is integral over $ R $, then $ x $ is integral over $ R $.

items.informal_name: The adjoined root of a monic polynomial is integral over the base semiring
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Ring S] {f : Polynomial R} [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  (h : IsAdjoinRootMonic S f), IsIntegral R h.root
items.informal_description: Given a commutative semiring $ R $, a semiring $ S $ with an $ R $-algebra structure obtained by adjoining a root of a monic polynomial $ f \in R[x] $, the adjoined root is integral over $ R $. This means there exists a monic polynomial with coefficients in $ R $ that annihilates the root, satisfying $ r_n x^n + r_{n-1} x^{n-1} + \dots + r_0 = 0 $ for some $ r_i \in R $ with $ r_n = 1 $.

items.informal_name: Root of a Monic Polynomial is Integral over the Base Ring
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {g : Polynomial R}, g.Monic → IsIntegral R (AdjoinRoot.root g)
items.informal_description: For any commutative ring $ R $ and monic polynomial $ g $ over $ R $, the root of $ g $ in the adjoin root ring $ R[X]/(g) $ is integral over $ R $. This means there exists a monic polynomial with coefficients in $ R $ (specifically $ g $ itself) that vanishes at this root, satisfying the definition of integrality.

items.informal_name: Minimal Polynomial of an Integral Element is Monic
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} {B : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : Ring B] [inst_2 : Algebra A B] {x : B},
  IsIntegral A x → (minpoly A x).Monic
items.informal_description: For an element $ x $ integral over a ring $ A $, the minimal polynomial $ \minpoly_A(x) $ is monic, meaning its leading coefficient is 1 in $ A $.
